clue.text: .Become whiter, not having left for the seaside

indicators.note: not having means the letter for left is dropped from the word

parts.note: to become whiter is to bleach

explanation.surface: A sunbather hoping to lighten up, but staying put at the seaside instead of leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' takes L out of BLEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach is the shore where people go for a day by the seaside, so the place stands for the resort trip.

clue.text: Be shown round a beat, in freshly-washed clothing

indicators.note: shown round means the letters of Be are placed around the next pieces like a tour guide

parts.note: taken as written
a beat or pulse is a throb

explanation.surface: Someone being given a tour of a police beat while wearing newly laundered clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown round' puts A THROB inside B...E.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathrobe is the garment put on after bathing, when one is freshly washed.

clue.text: Combining functions exhausted an individual

parts.note: all in is an idiom for exhausted or worn out
an individual is a single one

explanation.surface: A worn-out person juggling several duties at once.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-in-one device merges several functions into a single unit.

clue.text: Likely to succeed with own tracks, keeping hard at it over time

parts.note: to own something is to have it

indicators.note: keeping means the word for tracks holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: wakes are the tracks left behind boats in water

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the preceding pieces sit above the next one

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to a runner: with your own track to train on, keep at it hard over time and you will succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tracks' looks like railway lines or songs, but these are the trails boats leave; 'keeping' and 'over' arrange the pieces inside it, the latter meaning above in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has what it takes possesses the qualities needed, so is a likely success.

clue.text: Scared, with lion prowling? Not I!

definitions.text: Scared, with lion prowling? Not I!

indicators.note: prowling suggests restless movement, so these letters are moved around
Not I says the letter I is left out of the word lion

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone denies being frightened as a lion stalks nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes I from LION, leaving LON, and 'prowling' shuffles SCARED + LON. The whole clue is the hero's boast: in the fable the slave Androcles bravely pulled a thorn from a lion's paw.
explanation.definitionFit: Androcles is the figure from Aesop-style legend who fearlessly befriended a lion, so he could claim he was not the scared one.

clue.text: A major amount of capital needs to be put up as well

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are read upwards, back to front
a major amount of means most of the word, its final letter dropped

parts.note: Oslo is the capital of Norway

explanation.surface: Raising a large sum of money as well is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' points to the Norwegian city; 'major amount of' drops its final letter and 'put up' reads what is left upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Also is a plain synonym for as well, meaning in addition.

clue.text: An instrument of tragic queen, going about attempt to contain ominous uprising

indicators.note: going about means the queen's name wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: Dido, Queen of Carthage, killed herself when Aeneas left her

indicators.note: to contain means the word for attempt holds the next piece

parts.note: a go is an attempt

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means the word is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: dire means ominous or dreadful

explanation.surface: A tragic queen goes about attempting to suppress a threatening revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido was the Carthaginian queen in Virgil's Aeneid; 'going about' splits her name around the rest, 'to contain' and 'uprising' build that middle section.
explanation.definitionFit: The didgeridoo is a long wooden wind instrument of Aboriginal Australia.

clue.text: Unable to use tracks with no chance of success

definitions.meaning: literally a runner kept off the running track
idiomatically, no longer a contender in a race or competition

explanation.definitionFit: Out of the running literally means not in the race on the track, and figuratively having no hope of winning.

clue.text: Type of windows and doors displayed in gallery

definitions.meaning: a set of angled slats fitted in windows and doors
the great art museum in Paris

explanation.surface: Window and door designs shown in an art gallery exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A louvre is a slatted shutter for windows or doors, and the Louvre is the famous Paris art gallery.

clue.text: Eats late — has one had a few drinks?

definitions.meaning: late eats, a meal taken in the evening

definitions.text: has one had a few drinks?
definitions.meaning: one who sups is a drinker, so a person who has had a few drinks

explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, and whimsically a supper is someone who sups, or drinks.

clue.text: Appearing in film shot on the tube?

definitions.text: Appearing in film shot on the tube?

parts.words: Appearing in film shot on the tube?
parts.note: seems to describe a film made on the London Underground, but the tube is the television set

explanation.definitionFit: Something televised is broadcast on TV, informally called the tube.

clue.text: Tense, with' fit of depression following a blow.

indicators.note: following means the depression piece comes after the tense piece

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
the hump is British slang for a sulky, depressed mood

explanation.surface: Someone stressed and gloomy after being struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hump' is British slang for a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A thump is a heavy blow or punch.

clue.text: Never-ending price paid for living with personal fame

indicators.note: never-ending means the last letter is removed

parts.note: rent is the price paid for a place to live
own means personal, belonging to oneself

explanation.surface: Paying for lodgings forever while achieving personal celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is a synonym for fame or celebrity.

clue.text: Chap pulled out of the act, unavoidably

indicators.note: pulled out of means one word is removed from the other

parts.note: an act on stage is a performance
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A performer withdraws from a show because they have no choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled out of' removes MAN from PERFORMANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce is an old-fashioned adverb meaning necessarily or of necessity.

clue.text: I'm available to cope with deliveries on a one-off basis

definitions.text: I'm available to cope with deliveries on a one-off basis

parts.words: I'm available to cope with deliveries on a one-off basis
parts.note: reads like a temporary courier, but deliveries are balls bowled in cricket and the speaker is a substitute fielder

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the twelfth man is the reserve who fields when a team member is off, so handles the bowler's deliveries only occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket substitute fields in place of a player, handling bowled deliveries now and then.

clue.text: Fly below this in a fighter

definitions.text: Fly below this in a fighter

parts.words: Fly below this in a fighter
parts.note: suggests flying low in a fighter plane, but fly is the flyweight class of boxer, ranked under the class meant

explanation.walkthrough: Boxing weight classes run flyweight, then the next one up; a fighter here is a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantamweight is the boxing division immediately above flyweight.

clue.text: Gap in copy about to have tedious procedure held up

parts.note: to ape is to copy

indicators.note: to have means the word for about holds the next piece

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: A hole in a document caused by a boring delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reads the routine word upwards in this down entry, and 'to have' places it within the word for about.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is an opening or gap.

clue.text: Pile of combustibles Anne's — raked from the range

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of wood for burning

indicators.note: raked suggests the letters are scraped about and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Anne's bonfire heap gets raked over out on the range.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrenean describes something from the Pyrenees, the mountain range between France and Spain.

clue.text: Itemised research done when at Reading?

definitions.text: Itemised research done when at Reading?

parts.words: Itemised research done when at Reading?
parts.note: suggests study at Reading University, but means a list of books one has read

explanation.definitionFit: A bibliography is an itemised list of the books and sources used in research.

clue.text: Trendy, as well?

definitions.meaning: with something too, in addition to it

explanation.definitionFit: With it is slang for fashionable, and literally means along with something else, as well.

clue.text: Thanks French for quelling a kingdom, Anglo-Saxon

indicators.note: quelling means putting down, so in a down clue the first word sits on top of the next

parts.note: merci is French for thanks

explanation.surface: French gratitude helps subdue an old English realm.
explanation.walkthrough: MERCIA was a kingdom in the English Midlands in Anglo-Saxon times.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was one of the major kingdoms of Anglo-Saxon England.

clue.text: One's sometimes mistaken, trying to solve such an equation

definitions.meaning: who a person is, which can be wrongly assumed when someone is confused with another

definitions.text: trying to solve such an equation
definitions.meaning: an equation true for every value, so trying to solve it is pointless

explanation.definitionFit: Identity can be mistaken, and in maths an identity is an equation true for all values.

clue.text: Start off search, and regret being disloyal

indicators.note: start off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a hunt is a search
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone begins a search and comes to regret their betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue in the old sense means unfaithful or disloyal.

clue.text: Stop, without having finalised alliance

indicators.note: without having finalised means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: to block is to stop

explanation.surface: A halt to talks before an alliance is finalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without having finalised' drops the final K of BLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties joined in alliance.

clue.text: Poor writer has to include European diacritical mark

indicators.note: to include means the writer word holds the next piece

parts.note: a hack is a poor or mercenary writer

explanation.surface: A bad writer has to put in a European accent mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The hacek is the small inverted circumflex used over letters in Czech and other languages.

clue.text: Host required catering for large gathering

definitions.text: Host required catering for large gathering

parts.words: Host required catering for large gathering
parts.note: reads as a party host needing caterers, but the host is a huge crowd that itself is the large gathering

explanation.walkthrough: Host here means a great crowd, as in a heavenly host.
explanation.definitionFit: A multitude is a host or huge crowd of people, a large gathering.

clue.text: New boy, one enrolled in course, not ultimately particularly quick

indicators.note: enrolled in means these pieces go inside the course word
not ultimately means the course word loses its last letter

parts.note: a track is a course for racing
a son is a boy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A new pupil signs up for a course but is not, in the end, especially fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ultimately' sits after 'course' but trims it, not 'particularly quick'; 'enrolled in' puts the new boy and one inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Transonic describes speeds close to that of sound, so very quick indeed.

clue.text: Collect small pieces of good meat, with no fat

parts.note: lean meat is meat without fat

explanation.surface: Picking up scraps of fine fat-free meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bits gradually, as gleaners collect leftover grain.
